rubrics.justification: It correctly notes an expanded blastocyst with identifiable ICM and loose TE, but it over-interprets the image by claiming herniation, peripheral fragmentation, and cytoplasmic blebbing that are not clearly visible; the image quality and stage also make a confident downgrade to 3BB questionable.

It integrates age, tubal factor, prior ectopic/miscarriage, endometrium, sperm quality, BMI, and lifestyle with embryo assessment reasonably well, though some links (BMI, alcohol impact magnitude, AMH absence) are overstated.

The structure is logical and the probability estimate is internally explained, but several deductions are weak or speculative, especially the emphasis on Day 4 transfer asynchrony and large penalties assigned to alcohol/BMI/morphology.

Some recommendations are appropriate (early ectopic surveillance, review uterine/tubal factors), but others are not well guideline-based or are overstated, including routine aspirin suggestion, thrombophilia workup from this history alone, strong push for PGT-A, and framing Day 4 blastocyst transfer as a major synchrony problem.

It gives clear practical next steps for monitoring and future planning, especially regarding ectopic surveillance, though some actions are more aggressive than necessary and not all are evidence-based.
